findings.title: The film assembly grade adds a green cast to neutrals and sky, the direction of the 'olive' flaw that item D fixes
findings.evidence: assemble_track.py:23 applies `eq=contrast=1.04:saturation=1.06` to every shot. With the pipeline's own ffmpeg (6.1.1), eq with saturation != 1 maps neutral chroma 128 to 127 on both U and V. Test: lavfi grey 0x808080 yuv420p; `eq=saturation=1.06` gives U 127 / V 127, `null` and `eq=contrast=1.04` give 128 / 128. I ran synthetic sRGB patches through record3's exact encode, then the assemble per-shot chain (crf 18, bt709 tags), then a BT.709 decode (script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Calc/3fd08d73-28ea-592f-8f33-69ede4de867b/scratchpad/rv2r/pipe/tint.py). Results: (128,128,128)->(125,128,125); (60,60,60)->(54,57,54); (200,200,200)->(200,202,199); asphalt (154,141,126)->(153,141,123). The record3 encode alone stays within 1 level. On the 24 r2c frames r2/r2c_dep/fseq_d_roll_0_wb_*.png (script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Calc/3fd08d73-28ea-592f-8f33-69ede4de867b/scratchpad/rv2r/pipe/cmp.py): the shot mp4 decoded as BT.709 vs the PNGs has mean |d| 0.77, p99 4, signed (+0.13,+0.06,+0.11), so the encode itself is fine. After the film grade: mean |d| 2.46, signed (-1.69,+0.61,-1.74). Near-neutral pixels go from Duv +0.0043 to +0.0069. Sky top rows go from (204.5,215.5,223.3) Duv +0.0055 to (203.9,217.9,223.9) Duv +0.0069. README.md:32 keeps the grade as 'an output grade outside the engine'; the pipeline tests only checked the record3 encode, never neutrals through the eq.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop saturation from eq (keep contrast if wanted), or do the saturation with an explicitly rounded lutyuv around 128, or grade in RGB. Add a neutral-patch row (128/60/200 grey through the full record3 + assemble chain, |R-G|,|B-G| <= 1) to the pipeline test, and record the measured tint in the README.

findings.title: 777 fin from behind: the C1 pass (sat ratio 0.739) was measured on a different aircraft pose; in the film-config d_roll_0 frame the fin is still a cream/grey blade (ratio ~0.11)

In that frame the 777 is ~30 deg yawed to the camera, a rear-quarter view with the fin side visible. The r2c film-config still r2/r2c_dep/d_roll_0.png (wb=scene, aod 0.0405; log_dep.json: cam (1649,18,566.3), aircraft (1534.6,10,575.9) hdg -100.2) is directly behind. I masked the fin with a hand polygon (x 995-1022, y 362-585). Mean (177,173,170), HSV sat 0.041, hue 27 deg. Upper half (218,209,196): cream. The side-view fin in r2c_dep/d_gearup_0.png measures (129,177,212), sat 0.388, hue 206 deg. Ratio 0.11 against the plan's >= 0.6, hue off by ~180 deg. So the look-r1-look-1 'cream blade' persists in the film. CPU shader test (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Calc/3fd08d73-28ea-592f-8f33-69ede4de867b/scratchpad/rv2r/fin_cpu.mjs, sky_model.js skyRadianceCPU/modelLight at the logged geometry): incidence 82.7 deg; the mirror direction is az 252.5, el 2.7-5.4, 15-16 deg from the Sun; Schlick F 0.53; the coat reflection is 96% of the upper fin's radiance. The cream fin is therefore what the model predicts for this into-sun shot, plausibly physical, but nothing verifies it against a photograph. Root cause per the implementer's own A/B numbers: the base lobe (r1) moves sat 0.12->0.22 and the below-horizon environment (r2) 0.22->0.35; the normal flip is negligible (r2_oldnorm 0.338 vs 0.351). The doc's '0.465 / 0.463 ... base-lobe and old-normal variants' mislabels the data: 0.463 is r2_oldmat, and r2_oldnorm is 0.712.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-measure C1 on the film's actual d_roll frames, not the A/B harness pose, and correct environment_impl.md:1236. Either show with a reference photo (open licence) that a 777 fin seen from behind into a low sun reads pale, and close C1 as physical, or change the shot (camera/time) and mark the into-sun residual as an open question for the owner.

findings.title: United base massing: the Voronoi part extents contradict the roof sections visible on NAIP, and the new buildings are plain white boxes, so the 'placeholder hangar' look persists
findings.evidence: Own DOF parse of DOF.CSV (WGS 84 per the DOF_README 05-21-2026 I re-fetched) plus own OSM conversion. The 13 BLDG points, their AGL values and footprints match north_field.json, and parapet tops = 3 + AGL exactly (e.g. 35.61 for 06-035303's 107 ft), so the heights are right. The part EXTENTS are Voronoi cells (north_field_extract.py:13,89). The 107-ft point's cell is 13,825 m2 (near MAX_PART_M2 15,000), a 32.6-m block with diagonal step walls. On NAIP (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Calc/3fd08d73-28ea-592f-8f33-69ede4de867b/scratchpad/rv2r/nf_naip_b15.png) the Voronoi boundaries run diagonally across rectangular roof sections, sawtooth roofs and a dark lower roof. The observed roof breaks are available for measurement but were not used, as the r1b open question #3 itself proposed ('each NAIP roof section that contains a DOF point'). The renders r2/r2c_arr/nf_base_air.jpg and r2/r2c_dep2/d_gearup_100.png show B15 as a white diagonal-cut wedge. All nf_* units and the MOC film-facing faces (ENE/SSE, kept plain by design) read as featureless primer-white boxes, the B complaint, now in more places.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the footprints along NAIP-observed roof sections (obs), give each section the DOF top only where a point lies on it, and leave the others as the open owner question. Do not let one point's height fill a Voronoi cell. Get the owner's decision on question #3 before shipping; until then list B as not fixed for the films.
